name: Atlassian: suspend user access
description: Run from a case: find the case's user in your Atlassian organization by email and suspend their access to every Atlassian app (Jira, Confluence, ...) through the admin API. Their roles and groups come back when access is restored.

params.label: Organization ID
params.help: Shown when you create the API key (also in the admin.atlassian.com URL).

secrets.name: ATLASSIAN_ADMIN_API_KEY
secrets.description: Atlassian organization admin API key (sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`). Atlassian Administration > Settings > API keys.

setup:
### Atlassian side
1. admin.atlassian.com > **Settings > API keys > Create API key**. Use a key **without scopes** for now: Atlassian's scoped keys don't yet cover the v2 suspend endpoint (ID-9217). Keep it in Secrets only, and rotate it within a year.
2. Copy the **API key** and **Organization ID**.

### Case side
The user is the case's `username` attribute (custom artifact type) or its first email artifact.

### How it works
1. **Containment guard**: protected users and the caps in Settings > Integrations > Containment guardrails apply.
2. `POST /admin/v2/orgs/<org>/directories/-/users/search` with `{"emails": [<user>], "limit": 2}`: exactly one match is required.
3. `GET /admin/v2/orgs/<org>/directories?accountId=<id>`, then `POST /admin/v2/orgs/<org>/directories/<first directory>/users/<id>/suspend` (Atlassian answers **204**). An org with several directories gets the first one suspended; the note lists how many there are.
4. A note records the statuses; run from a case task, the task gets the result and is ticked on success.

Undo: admin.atlassian.com > Directory > Users > the user > **Restore access** (or `POST .../users/<id>/restore`).

Docs relied on:
- Admin API keys: https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/manage-an-organization-with-the-admin-apis/
- Organization REST API (OpenAPI): https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/admin/organization/rest/intro/
